scope: Targeted recheck of the Round 1 fixes (rows_fixes.json, census_dry.json) and a first read of RNEW/rows.json (22 source items, 4 held items, 17 omissions)

findings.target: rows_fixes.json held_class (dry run of the recommended rule)
findings.problem: The rule as applied says reported and attributed sources don't count, for source and held items alike. But held_class tags only the five reported held rows. The four held rows that Round 1 classed as attributed are still counted in census_dry.json. Theodosius I's attributed row is now replaced by RNEW's letter, so three remain: Marutha of Maypherqat (persian-church-of-the-east-early; the Nicene texts are 'attributed to' him), Severus ibn al-Muqaffa' (coptic-christianity-under-early-islam; the History's attribution is contested, as R36's own reason says) and Elsbeth Stagel (rhineland-mysticism-and-the-friends-of-god; she is 'credited with' the sister-book). Source items marked attributed (Pamphilus, Gerard) were excluded, so the dry run treats the two kinds of item differently.
findings.evidence: census_dry.json people: persian-church-of-the-east-early includes Marutha (held); coptic-christianity-under-early-islam = [Severus ibn al-Muqaffa'] (held); rhineland includes Elsbeth Stagel (held). Round 1 held_check kind 'attributed' for all three. Shelf notes and work titles say 'attributed to' or 'credited with'.
findings.fix: Add the three to held_class as 'attributed'. Then coptic-christianity-under-early-islam has no one left and needs a people note. A suggestion, which only repeats what R36 says: 'No one is shown. The History of the Patriarchs is linked to Severus, but whether he wrote it is disputed.' If Mark rules that attributed held rows count, record that ruling instead.

findings.problem: 'Bar Sauma's journey is the one account of its people in the Library' claims more than any source behind it. The shelf also holds Hetum, Malech, Cathay and the Way Thither and the RHC Armenian documents, and the original reason made no such claim. 'Its people' is also vague.
findings.evidence: cic/corpus-map/church-of-the-east-under-the-mongols.yaml authors: cathay-and-the-way-thither, hetum, malech, rhc-armeniens, yahballaha-sauma. R36 decision: 'the row is an anonymous Syriac abridgment of his own Persian account'.
findings.fix: For example: 'No one is shown. Bar Sauma's own account of his journey survives only as another writer retold it.'

findings.problem: 'no real author stands behind them' says these books had no real author. The original said only that no named person stands behind them. They had authors; the authors are unnamed, or wrote under a borrowed name.
findings.evidence: R12 original: 'These are anonymous and pseudonymous texts, so no named person stands behind any of them.'
findings.fix: 'No one is shown. These books carry no author's name, or a borrowed one, so no real author can be named.'

findings.problem: 'lay people who lived and worked together' adds a claim the original did not make. It is also not true of the whole movement: the entry says the third order was married lay people 'who stayed in ordinary working life'.
findings.evidence: R36 original: 'a lay collective with no named founder or leader on record'. The voices line: 'a lay collective, organized by trade and locality'.
findings.fix: 'No one is shown. The Humiliati were groups of lay people, organized by trade and town, and no founder or leader is named on record.'

findings.problem: 'so no one here is shown in his own words yet' implies the people are shown some other way, and 'his' assumes everyone named is a man. It also doesn't follow the 'No one is shown.' pattern of the rewritten notes.
findings.evidence: RNEW/rows.json empty_reasons; the five decisions all say the words are reported by a Jesuit in the Relations.
findings.fix: 'No one is shown. The people named here speak in the Library only through the Jesuits who wrote their words down.'

checked: Fixes: every patched or added quote re-verified verbatim by script (5/5). Each item checked in census_dry.json. All 26 rewritten notes read against their originals and voices lines. I also checked that the dry run applies the recommended rule the same way to source and held items (it does not: R2-F1). RNEW: all 22 source quotes verbatim at their lines (22/22). I opened the text around every quote to confirm the speaker. The 4 held rows exist with matching author slugs. Names are substrings of their voices lines in census_dry.json, except Maurice Chauncy, whose movement exists only in D2/Draft.json and not in Draft_optionA.json; he matches D2/Draft.json voices[3]. That depends on Mark's ruling on the option, not a defect. Rows are in year order. I read all 17 omissions. They are consistent with the rule: New France and Houghton are excluded as reported speech, Methley and Tregoose as attributed, the rest have no words of their own in the Library.
